pictures.observed: Long limestone elevation, large glazed upper bays, deeply recessed lower slit windows and small parapet recesses. Glazed circulation towers are visible farther along the range. The road and the order of the volumes suggest the north-facing eastern bay assignment.
Hillside elevation with tall glazed stairs, projecting pale piers, a long central curtain wall and a thin roof rail. It shows the roof stepping across the adjoining volumes.
New seminars wing next to the museum exit, with two continuous bands of glazing, a roof overhang and a pale end wall. Relative site position ties the wing to the western end of the range.

Overhead imagery corroborates the bent footprint, changes of roof plane, and a separate rectangular building to the south. Provider imagery has visible parallax and is used to identify features. PMTiles supplies the model footprint.

attribution: Tafnit, International Business Times and Esri imagery contributors. Reference images viewed only.
limitations: Facade placement and visible height are inferred from the order of volumes in the exterior photographs and overhead view. Roof equipment, rear bays, and facade counts are approximate.
The separate study wing, detached retaining walls, bridge connections between buildings, and interior rooms remain outside this asset.
